info.title: kda-indexer chainweb-data compatible API
info.description: The REST routes of chainweb-data (txs, account transfers, events, search, /coins, /stats) and the /v1/txs convenience route, served by the compat listener (api.compat). Shapes, error texts and row order follow chainweb-data; documented differences are listed per route. JSON uses chainweb-data's camelCase names and aeson's number and time text. Errors are plain text. List routes (/txs/account, /txs/events, /txs/search) take limit (default 10, capped at 250), offset (up to 10,000) or a next token, minheight and maxheight, and answer a JSON array with the next page's token in the Chainweb-Next header. Genesis transactions are hidden on the list routes. Every data route answers 429 (per-client rate), 503 (too many requests in flight, or an answer over api.max_body_mb) and 504 (the 5 s deadline; /v1/txs has its own 30 s deadline, slot pool and body cap, see the route). Search routes run under a shared gate (503 when search.concurrency searches run; past search.per_client a client's searches wait their turn, 429 only when 3 more already wait). CORS is open and Chainweb-Next and X-Count-Age are exposed.

get.description:
chainweb-data `coinsHandler`: the circulating KDA at the highest stored height and the
current time, printed as the Haskell `show` of a `Decimal` (`text/plain`, for example
`1234567.89`). The supply tables are mainnet01's: any other network, like an empty
store, answers `404 Server database is empty`.

404.description: `Server database is empty` (empty store, or a network other than mainnet01)

429.description:
The per-client request rate (`api.rate_per_ip`, `api.rate_burst`) is used up, or, on a
search route, the client already runs `search.per_client` searches and has 3 more
waiting (a search past `search.per_client` waits its turn, it is not refused). Retry
after the `Retry-After` seconds.

500.description: A read failed; the cause is logged, the body is `internal error`.

503.description:
`api.max_in_flight` requests are running, the answer would exceed `api.max_body_mb`
(`response larger than N MB: narrow the query`), `search.concurrency` searches are
running, or (on `/stats`) the first count is not ready. On `/txs/events`, `/txs/search`
and `/v1/txs`, which take a per-client heavy-read slot, a client that already runs one
heavy request and has others waiting is refused too (`this client already runs a heavy
request and has others waiting: retry when they are done`). Search refusals, the
heavy-read refusal and `/stats` carry `Retry-After`; the in-flight and body-size
refusals do not.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait; absent on the in-flight and body-size refusals.

504.description:
The request ran past `api.deadline_ms` (5 s by default): `request deadline exceeded`.
On a search route, a search still waiting behind the client's earlier ones at the
deadline answers `request deadline exceeded while waiting for this client's earlier
searches`, with `Retry-After: 1`.

get.description:
chainweb-data `statsHandler`: `{"transactionCount": N, "coinsInCirculation": X}`, the
exact user-transaction count. A background task recounts, each count starting two
minutes after the previous one ended and running to completion; a request never
recounts and answers the last count with `X-Count-Age` (seconds since that count
started; every 200 has it). Before the first count exists the request waits up to the
deadline, then answers `503` with `Retry-After: 5`. A failed recount keeps the last
count and its age grows. `coinsInCirculation` is mainnet01's supply table; other
networks answer `404 Server database is empty`.

X-Count-Age.description: Seconds since the count started; readable by browsers (CORS exposed).

404.description: `Server database is empty` (empty store, or a network other than mainnet01)

get.description:
chainweb-data `accountHandler`: a JSON array of `TransferDetail`, newest first (height
descending, request key descending, event index ascending), the rows of `token` (default
`coin`) with the account on either side. A transfer to oneself is one row. Pages carry
`Chainweb-Next` when there is more. Genesis transactions are hidden; miner rewards are
listed. A chain id outside 0..=19, an unknown account or token answers an empty array; a `chain` past a 64-bit integer is a 400.
`amount` is the shortest exact decimal text, so it differs from chainweb-data's raw
text (`"138000"` for `"138000.000000000000"`) while being the same decimal.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: Account name, 1 to 256 bytes.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Fungible module of the transfers (default `coin`).

parameters.name: chain
parameters.description: Only this chain (0 to 19); another whole number answers an empty page, a number beyond a 64-bit integer is a 400.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Page size, an integer (servant's `Integer`: a sign then digits). Default 10; a value
above 250 is capped to 250. A negative value answers `500 Something went wrong`
(chainweb-data passes it to SQL `LIMIT`). Anything else that is not an integer is
`400 Error parsing query parameter limit failed: could not parse: ...`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description:
Rows to skip, default 0, at most 10,000 (more answers `400`; page further with
`next`). A negative value counts as 0. Not allowed together with `next`.

parameters.name: next
parameters.description:
The `Chainweb-Next` token of the previous page. Tokens are kda-indexer cursors;
treat them as opaque. A token chainweb-data issued is accepted too and resumes on
the page chainweb-data serves after it (chainweb-data does not accept ours). A token
that does not decode is `400 Invalid next token: ...`; with `offset` it is
`400 next token query parameter not allowed with offset`.

parameters.name: minheight
parameters.description: Lowest block height (inclusive).

parameters.name: maxheight
parameters.description:
Highest block height (inclusive). A negative value, or `minheight` above
`maxheight`, answers an empty page.

parameters.name: Chainweb-Execution-Strategy
parameters.description: Accepted and ignored. Any other value is `400 Unknown Chainweb-Execution-Strategy: ...`.

Chainweb-Next.description: Token of the next page (pass as `next`); absent on the last page.

400.description: A parameter does not parse (`Error parsing query parameter ...`), `offset` above 10,000, `next` with `offset`, or an invalid `next`

get.description:
chainweb-data `evHandler`: a JSON array of `EventDetail`, newest first (height
descending, request key descending, event index ascending). Filters combine with AND:
`modulename` is an exact module, `name` a SQL `LIKE '%name%'` on the qualified name,
`param` a `LIKE` on the parameters' JSON text, `search` a `LIKE` on either. Patterns
take `%` and `_`, `\` escapes them, at most 256 characters and 8 `%`. Without
`modulename`, `name` and `param` need at least `search.min_len` (4) characters other
than wildcards and may take a bounded newest-first scan (`search.max_scan_heights`,
`search.timeout_ms`): a cut scan answers what it found with `X-Search-Truncated: true`
and `Chainweb-Next`. `search` takes one slot of the search gate (`503` when
`search.concurrency` searches run, `429` when the client already runs
`search.per_client`). Genesis transactions are hidden.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: LIKE pattern matched against the qualified name or the parameter text.

parameters.name: param
parameters.description: LIKE pattern matched against the parameter text (JSON).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: LIKE pattern matched against the qualified event name, for example `coin.TRANSFER`.

parameters.name: modulename
parameters.description: Exact module name, for example `coin`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Page size, an integer (servant's `Integer`: a sign then digits). Default 10; a value
above 250 is capped to 250. A negative value answers `500 Something went wrong`
(chainweb-data passes it to SQL `LIMIT`). Anything else that is not an integer is
`400 Error parsing query parameter limit failed: could not parse: ...`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description:
Rows to skip, default 0, at most 10,000 (more answers `400`; page further with
`next`). A negative value counts as 0. Not allowed together with `next`.

parameters.name: next

parameters.description: Lowest block height (inclusive).

parameters.name: maxheight
parameters.description:
Highest block height (inclusive). A negative value, or `minheight` above
`maxheight`, answers an empty page.

parameters.description: Accepted and ignored. Any other value is `400 Unknown Chainweb-Execution-Strategy: ...`.

get.description:
chainweb-data `recentTxsHandler`: a JSON array of up to ten `TxSummary`, newest height
first. Inside one height chainweb-data leaves the order to Postgres; here it is request
key descending. Genesis and coinbase transactions are left out. The walk looks at most
20,000 heights back, so a store whose newest heights hold no user transactions answers
fewer than ten.

get.summary: Search transactions by code, or list a defpact
get.description:
chainweb-data `searchTxs`. Exactly one of `search` and `pactid`: neither answers
`404 You must specify a search string`, both `400 You should only specify a pactid or a
search string, not both!`.

`search`: a JSON array of `TxSummary` for the transactions whose own exec code contains
the pattern (a `LIKE` pattern: `%`, `_`, `\` escapes; at most 256 characters and 8 `%`),
height descending then request key descending. A pattern with a literal run of 3
characters uses the code index; when the index may miss matches (fallback mode below its
length threshold, or it trails the tip) its verified hits are served with
`X-Search-Truncated: true`. With no index hit, or no 3-character run, a bounded
newest-first scan runs (`search.max_scan_heights`, `search.timeout_ms`). A cut
answer carries `X-Search-Truncated: true` and, when there is more, `Chainweb-Next`.
Genesis transactions are listed here (the other list routes hide them). Difference from
chainweb-data: its `cont` transactions also match through the initial code of their
defpact; here they do not. The route takes one slot of the search gate (`503` when
`search.concurrency` searches run, `429` when the client already runs `search.per_client`).

`pactid`: the `cont` transactions of the defpact (the starting transaction excluded),
successful ones first, then height descending (ties: request key ascending), at most 50.
Only the newest 1,000 transactions of the pact are read, so an old successful
continuation of a pact with more transactions may be missing; such an answer carries
`X-Search-Truncated: true`. Height and paging parameters are ignored and no
`Chainweb-Next` is sent, as in chainweb-data. A value that is not a pact id matches
nothing (an empty array).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: LIKE pattern matched against the exec code.

parameters.name: pactid
parameters.description: Defpact id (base64url hash); the `limit` is capped at 50.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Page size, an integer (servant's `Integer`: a sign then digits). Default 10; a value
above 250 is capped to 250. A negative value answers `500 Something went wrong`
(chainweb-data passes it to SQL `LIMIT`). Anything else that is not an integer is
`400 Error parsing query parameter limit failed: could not parse: ...`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description:
Rows to skip, default 0, at most 10,000 (more answers `400`; page further with
`next`). A negative value counts as 0. Not allowed together with `next`.

parameters.name: next
parameters.description:
The `Chainweb-Next` token of the previous page. Tokens are kda-indexer cursors;
treat them as opaque. A token chainweb-data issued is accepted too and resumes on
the page chainweb-data serves after it (chainweb-data does not accept ours). A token
that does not decode is `400 Invalid next token: ...`; with `offset` it is
`400 next token query parameter not allowed with offset`.

parameters.name: minheight
parameters.description: Lowest block height (inclusive).

parameters.name: maxheight
parameters.description:
Highest block height (inclusive). A negative value, or `minheight` above
`maxheight`, answers an empty page.

parameters.name: Chainweb-Execution-Strategy
parameters.description: Accepted and ignored. Any other value is `400 Unknown Chainweb-Execution-Strategy: ...`.

Chainweb-Next.description: Token of the next page (`search` only); absent on the last page.

X-Search-Truncated.description: `true` when the scan deadline or a cap cut the answer short, or the code index served hits that may not be every match (fallback mode, lag).

400.description: Both `search` and `pactid`, a parameter that does not parse, a pattern that is too long or has too many `%`, `offset` above 10,000, `next` with `offset`, or an invalid `next`

404.description: `You must specify a search string`: neither `search` nor `pactid`

get.summary: The transactions behind an account's newest transfers
get.description:
The newest `limit` transfer rows of the account in `namespace` (the fungible module,
default `coin`) and the transactions that made them, as `TxDetail` records (the shape of
`/txs/txs`). Each path segment is optional and falls back to the query parameter of the
same name: `/v1/txs/{account}/{namespace}/{limit}` equals
`/v1/txs?account=...&namespace=...&limit=...`. Rows of the token come first and, for a
token other than `coin`, the account's `coin` rows follow. A transaction with several
matching rows appears once, at its first row; miner rewards count toward `limit` but
produce no entry. `limit` follows JavaScript `Number()` (hex, exponent and fractions
parse; an empty, zero or non-numeric value means the default 50; above 10,000 it is
capped, before its fraction is looked at). A negative value, or a fractional one up to
10,000, is `404 Not Found`, as is a fourth path segment. A missing account is
`400 Bad Request`. Genesis transactions are hidden. The answer is capped at
`api.v1txs_max_body_mb` (32 MB by default; `503` past it, use a smaller `limit`).

The read has its own time budget and slot pool, apart from the other routes: it runs for
up to `api.v1txs_deadline_ms` (30 s by default; `504` past it, where kda-txs answers 404)
on one of a quarter of `api.read_threads` slots (at least one), and waits at most
`api.deadline_ms` (5 s) for a slot (`503`). The server answers after up to 35 s, so a
balancer in front needs a server timeout of 40 s or more for this route.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: Account name (required: without it `400 Bad Request`).

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.description: Fungible module.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Transfer rows to read: a JavaScript number, default 50, capped at 10,000.

404.description: `Not Found`: a negative `limit`, a fractional `limit` up to 10,000, or more than three path segments

429.description:
The per-client request rate (`api.rate_per_ip`, `api.rate_burst`) is used up. Retry
after the `Retry-After` seconds.

500.description: A read failed; the cause is logged, the body is `internal error`.

503.description:
Refused: `api.max_in_flight` requests are running; no `/v1/txs` slot freed within
`api.deadline_ms` (5 s by default), `too many /v1/txs requests running: retry later`;
the client already runs a heavy request and has others waiting (`this client already
runs a heavy request and has others waiting: retry when they are done`, the only one
with `Retry-After: 1`); or the answer is larger than `api.v1txs_max_body_mb`
(`response larger than N MB: use a smaller limit`).

504.description:
The read ran past `api.v1txs_deadline_ms` (30 s by default):
`request deadline exceeded`. kda-txs answers 404 at that point.

get.summary: The transactions behind an account's newest transfers, path form
get.description:
The same route as `/v1/txs`, with the parameters as path segments. The trailing
segments may be left out (`/v1/txs/{account}` and `/v1/txs/{account}/{namespace}` are
served; OpenAPI cannot describe optional path segments, so only the full form is
listed). An empty segment falls back to the query parameter of the same name.

Limits as for `/v1/txs`: the read has its own time budget (`api.v1txs_deadline_ms`, 30 s
by default; `504` past it) and slot pool (a quarter of `api.read_threads`, at least one;
`503` when none frees within `api.deadline_ms`). A balancer in front needs a server
timeout of 40 s or more for this route.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: Account name.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.description: Fungible module (`coin` when empty).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Transfer rows to read: a JavaScript number, default 50, capped at 10,000.

404.description: `Not Found`: a negative `limit`, a fractional `limit` up to 10,000, or more than three path segments

429.description:
The per-client request rate (`api.rate_per_ip`, `api.rate_burst`) is used up. Retry
after the `Retry-After` seconds.

500.description: A read failed; the cause is logged, the body is `internal error`.

503.description:
Refused: `api.max_in_flight` requests are running; no `/v1/txs` slot freed within
`api.deadline_ms` (5 s by default), `too many /v1/txs requests running: retry later`;
the client already runs a heavy request and has others waiting (`this client already
runs a heavy request and has others waiting: retry when they are done`, the only one
with `Retry-After: 1`); or the answer is larger than `api.v1txs_max_body_mb`
(`response larger than N MB: use a smaller limit`).

504.description:
The read ran past `api.v1txs_deadline_ms` (30 s by default):
`request deadline exceeded`. kda-txs answers 404 at that point.

transactionCount.description: Exact user-transaction count, as of `X-Count-Age` seconds ago.

coinsInCirculation.description: Circulating KDA; null when the supply table has no value for the height.

idx.description: Event index, ordered with the other rows of the same transaction.

crossChainAccount.description:
The other side of a cross-chain transfer, from the `TRANSFER_XCHAIN` / `X_RESUME`
events of the same transaction.

amount.description:
Decimal text, shortest exact form (`"138000"`, not `"138000.000000000000"`): equal
as a decimal to chainweb-data's, different as a string.

gasPrice.description: The gas price as a JSON number (aeson `Double`).

data.description: The payload data (exec or cont), any JSON.

result.description: The result data on success, the error on failure.

txid.description: Pact transaction id (0 when the node gave none).

blockTime.description: Block creation time, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.ffffff]Z` (fraction without trailing zeros).

initialCode.description: Code of the transaction that started the defpact, for a continuation.

previousSteps.description: Earlier steps of the defpact, for a continuation.
